curated.author: Wei Ling
curated.note: Day 9, first pins on the oyster kit. Tiny white dots along the slit, exactly like the guide said.

timeline.note: Mixed one part spawn to four parts grounds, sealed the bag, put it in the cupboard.
Fully colonised and the first slit is fruiting. Mist twice a day from here.

curated.note: Mixed into the topsoil of the three pothos on the windowsill. The soil finally holds water instead of running straight through.

curated.author: Farah Idris
curated.note: Two days drying on the balcony ledge, then a jam jar with holes punched in the lid. My mum asked for a jar for her chillies.
Half a bag of shredded paper, one turn with the fork, and the pile is warm again two days later.

Keep grounds 3 cm clear of the stem. Mine went mouldy in the first week because I piled them right up against it.

curated.author: Daniel Ong
curated.note: Does decaf work for mushrooms? The L8 machine is decaf after 3pm and I have a spare kit.

replies.body: Used decaf twice, colonised fine, maybe a day slower.
Same here. Give it 12 days instead of 10 and you cannot tell the difference.

curated.note: Collected 240 g on Tuesday, dried it in the pantry overnight, took it home in a paper bag.

curated.author: Jun Wei
curated.note: The balcony bin is finally doing the work by itself instead of me.

timeline.note: Grounds and browns layered 1:3 into the balcony bin.
Pile at 48°C this morning, first turn done. Smells like forest floor, not rubbish.

curated.note: The office fig has been sulking since July. Two weeks of grounds and there are four new leaves.
Only fully dry grounds in the fridge. I tried it wet once and came back to a science experiment.

curated.author: Priya Raman
curated.note: Second flush from the same block, smaller caps but just as many. Harvested 180 g for dinner.
Has anyone cured a bar for longer than 24 hours? Mine still crumbles at the edges.

replies.body: A week works better. Wrap it in baking paper first and leave it in a cupboard.
Mine crumbled until I ground the grounds coarser. Might not be the cure time at all.

curated.note: Sprinkled a thin layer over the herb pots — basil, mint, two chillies. The mint has gone feral.
Took the whole caddy's worth before clear-out on Thursday. Nothing from L9 went to waste that week.
Took 184 g home in a jar, and no photo of the jar because it mostly looked like mud.
The kit lives under my desk in a box. Colleagues keep asking what is in it.

curated.author: Ravi Menon
curated.note: One pouch in the fridge, one in the shoe cupboard. The cupboard one is doing more work, honestly.
Watered the grounds in properly this time. Last batch I left them dry on top and they just sat there.

curated.author: Mei Lim
curated.note: Is anyone else's pile going cold after the second turn? Mine dropped to 30°C overnight.

replies.body: Add more browns and cover it. Ours did exactly the same in the rain.
Too wet. Leave the lid off for a day and turn it again on Thursday.

curated.note: Two moulds poured and cut, and the kitchen smelled like a coffee shop all afternoon.

timeline.note: Melted the base, stirred in 5% grounds, poured two moulds.
Cured and cut. The bars hold together properly this time.

curated.author: Hafiz Rahman
curated.note: Oyster mushrooms on toast, day eleven. My flatmate asked which shop I bought them from.
Ferns love it. The ones in the lobby planter have doubled since September.
How often is everyone replacing theirs? The guide says three weeks but mine smells of nothing after ten days.

replies.body: Three weeks if you stir it. Ten days if you do not.

curated.note: The community garden down the road took 2 kg off my hands and asked for more every Tuesday.
Bring your own jar. The kraft pouches leak through the bottom by the time you reach the MRT.
Third flush is a stretch. Two good ones and the block goes into the compost.

curated.author: Anna Lim
curated.note: Made six bars and left four in the L12 pantry with a note. They were gone by lunch.
The tomato plants on the balcony are the beneficiaries this week. Two more trusses than last year.

curated.author: Chloe Tan
curated.note: Started a 40 L bin on the balcony and it is already halfway to soil.

timeline.note: Grounds, dry leaves and cardboard into a 40 L bin.
Turned once, no smell, and the worms have moved in. Half the volume already.

curated.note: Dried on the office window ledge behind the printer. Two days, bone dry, no smell in the room.

curated.author: Wei Ling
curated.note: Ours fruited sideways out of the slit. Do I turn the block around or leave it?

replies.body: Leave it. They grow toward the light either way and turning it breaks the pins.
Leave it and rotate the box a quarter turn next flush, not this one.

curated.note: Roses, of all things. The grounds went straight into the bed at my parents' place.
Third week running. The bin is at 52°C and the neighbours have stopped asking about the smell.
Gave one bar to the barista downstairs. He asked for the recipe, which I took as a compliment.

curated.author: Farah Idris
curated.note: First kit from the L9 pantry grounds, and it actually worked.

timeline.note: Mixed 1 part spawn to 4 parts grounds and sealed the bag.
Fully white, cut the first slit this morning.

curated.note: Weighed in at 267 g on Tuesday. Best week yet on L14.
Used the dried grounds on the succulents after all, thin layer, and they are fine three weeks on.
The pile finally hit 55°C. Three weeks of grounds and browns and it is doing the work itself now.
Two trays dried on the balcony and a full jar in the fridge. The pantry one smells like a cafe now.
